quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After you complete the turn, your car should be:

options.text: In the center of the street.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, complete your turn into the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can drive under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed you can drive under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed to drive under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can drive under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, and bad weather. If road or weather conditions make the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb on a two-way street, you must:

options.text: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.
Place your right rear tire on the curb.
Leave your car six inches from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on the right side of a street with a curb, turn your wheels to the left and let your car roll back so the front right tire touches the curb. This stops your vehicle from rolling into traffic if your brakes fail.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means drivers next to it can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines are placed in the center of roads to separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. You should:

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
Wait for police before moving your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if you can. Do not leave the accident scene without identifying yourself and helping if needed.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination quickly.
Drive closer to the car ahead.
Stay further away from the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay further away from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. You should:

options.text: Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to let drivers know you are waiting.
Drive around a car that is blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another vehicle hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far your vehicle travels before stopping?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with speed and road conditions. Steering ability does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: You can only make a U-turn if you can see for at least this distance in both directions:
questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn where you cannot see or be seen for at least 500 feet in both directions. Do not make U-turns near the top of hills or inside curves.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right. This rule applies at all intersections, whether they have signs, signals, or no markings.

questions.question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Maintain a constant speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve, then gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up as you enter a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch carefully for other vehicles.

questions.question: When you cannot see clearly while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: When visibility is reduced, your first action should be to slow down. This gives you more time to react to hazards.

questions.question: If you are convicted of driving without proper insurance, how long must you carry SR-22 insurance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three years.
questions.explanation: If you are convicted of driving without insurance or without proof of insurance, you must carry SR-22 insurance for three years. You will also have to pay a $45 reinstatement fee.

questions.question: When you first get in a car to drive, what should you adjust first?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat first so you are comfortable and can see the road. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your seat position.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones are marked with orange signs with black lettering. Always slow down and stay alert in work zones.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to look over your shoulder before every lane change. This is the best way to check your blind spots.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem are traveling at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: When can you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for other traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following, except:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect your BAC.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
May no longer turn and must proceed straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer have to turn in the direction the arrow indicated.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow turns to a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow, you should:

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and expect oncoming traffic to stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is about to appear. Stop your vehicle unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when:

options.text: Stopping on a wet or icy road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping on a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distances increase on wet or icy roads. Stopping distances also increase on loose gravel or stones.
